snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, p.project_name, ep.emp_id FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Projects p ON d.dept_id = p.dept_id LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id;

snapshot.title: Filter four-table join: High earners working on completed projects
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, e.salary, d.dept_name, and p.project_name by joining Employees, Departments, Employee_Projects, and Projects where p.status = 'Completed' AND e.salary > 40000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.salary, d.dept_name, p.project_name FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id WHERE p.status = 'Completed' AND e.salary > 40000;

snapshot.title: Filter four-table join: Heavy commitments (> 25 hrs) on active initiatives
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, d.location, p.project_name, and ep.hours_allocated by joining Employees, Departments, Employee_Projects, and Projects where ep.hours_allocated > 25 AND p.status = 'Active'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, d.location, p.project_name, ep.hours_allocated FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id WHERE ep.hours_allocated > 25 AND p.status = 'Active';

snapshot.title: Synthesize complete profile: Employee, department, project, and review rating
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, d.dept_name, p.project_name, and pr.rating by joining Employees, Departments, Employee_Projects, Projects, and Performance_Reviews where pr.review_year = 2024.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, d.dept_name, p.project_name, pr.rating FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id WHERE pr.review_year = 2024;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Find unique pairs of employees working in the same department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e1.emp_name AS employee_1, e2.emp_name AS employee_2, and e1.department by self-joining Employees on department where e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS employee_1, e2.emp_name AS employee_2, e1.department FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.department = e2.department WHERE e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Find colleague pairings sharing the same office city
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e1.emp_name AS colleague_1, e2.emp_name AS colleague_2, and e1.city by self-joining Employees on city where e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS colleague_1, e2.emp_name AS colleague_2, e1.city FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.city = e2.city WHERE e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Identify departmental colleagues where one out-earns the other by >= 20000
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e1.emp_name AS higher_earner, e1.salary AS high_sal, e2.emp_name AS lower_earner, e2.salary AS low_sal, and e1.department by self-joining Employees on department where e1.salary >= e2.salary + 20000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS higher_earner, e1.salary AS high_sal, e2.emp_name AS lower_earner, e2.salary AS low_sal, e1.department FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.department = e2.department WHERE e1.salary >= e2.salary + 20000;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Pair employees hired in the same calendar year
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e1.emp_name AS joiner_1, e2.emp_name AS joiner_2, and e1.joining_year by self-joining Employees on joining_year where e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS joiner_1, e2.emp_name AS joiner_2, e1.joining_year FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.joining_year = e2.joining_year WHERE e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Pair projects belonging to the same department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display p1.project_name AS project_1, p2.project_name AS project_2, and p1.dept_id by self-joining Projects on dept_id where p1.project_id < p2.project_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p1.project_name AS project_1, p2.project_name AS project_2, p1.dept_id FROM Projects p1 INNER JOIN Projects p2 ON p1.dept_id = p2.dept_id WHERE p1.project_id < p2.project_id;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Track year-over-year rating progression for the same employee
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Performance_Reviews to display r1.emp_id, r1.review_year AS prev_year, r1.rating AS prev_rating, r2.review_year AS next_year, and r2.rating AS next_rating by self-joining on emp_id where r1.review_year = r2.review_year - 1.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT r1.emp_id, r1.review_year AS prev_year, r1.rating AS prev_rating, r2.review_year AS next_year, r2.rating AS next_rating FROM Performance_Reviews r1 INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews r2 ON r1.emp_id = r2.emp_id WHERE r1.review_year = r2.review_year - 1;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Pair colleagues with identical years of professional experience
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e1.emp_name AS peer_1, e2.emp_name AS peer_2, and e1.experience by self-joining Employees on experience where e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS peer_1, e2.emp_name AS peer_2, e1.experience FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.experience = e2.experience WHERE e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Self-join: Identify pairs of employees collaborating on the same project
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employee_Projects to display ep1.project_id, ep1.emp_id AS team_member_1, and ep2.emp_id AS team_member_2 by self-joining on project_id where ep1.emp_id < ep2.emp_id.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT ep1.project_id, ep1.emp_id AS team_member_1, ep2.emp_id AS team_member_2 FROM Employee_Projects ep1 INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep2 ON ep1.project_id = ep2.project_id WHERE ep1.emp_id < ep2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Cross join: Generate all theoretical department and project status combinations
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to generate a Cartesian product between distinct dept_name from Departments and distinct status from Projects. Alias columns as dept_name and project_status.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, s.status AS project_status FROM (SELECT DISTINCT dept_name FROM Departments) d CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT status FROM Projects) s;

snapshot.title: Cross join: Generate branch city and department combinations
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display distinct city from Employees paired with distinct dept_name from Departments using CROSS JOIN.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT c.city, d.dept_name FROM (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM Employees) c CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT dept_name FROM Departments) d;

snapshot.title: Cross join with scalar aggregate: Compare each employee's salary to company average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, e.salary, a.avg_sal, and (e.salary - a.avg_sal) AS salary_diff by CROSS JOINing Employees with a subquery calculating ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_sal from Employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.salary, a.avg_sal, (e.salary - a.avg_sal) AS salary_diff FROM Employees e CROSS JOIN (SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_sal FROM Employees) a;

snapshot.title: Cross join with total capital: Compute each project's percentage share of portfolio budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display p.project_name, p.budget, and ROUND((p.budget * 100.0) / t.total_budget, 2) AS budget_pct by CROSS JOINing Projects with a subquery computing SUM(budget) AS total_budget from Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, p.budget, ROUND((p.budget * 100.0) / t.total_budget, 2) AS budget_pct FROM Projects p CROSS JOIN (SELECT SUM(budget) AS total_budget FROM Projects) t;

snapshot.title: Cross join: Generate rating evaluation slots (1 to 5) for all corporate departments
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display d.dept_name and r.rating_slot by CROSS JOINing (SELECT DISTINCT dept_name FROM Departments) d with (SELECT DISTINCT rating AS rating_slot FROM Performance_Reviews) r.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, r.rating_slot FROM (SELECT DISTINCT dept_name FROM Departments) d CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT rating AS rating_slot FROM Performance_Reviews) r;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Aggregate headcount and total payroll joined with department budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS emp_count, SUM(e.salary) AS total_payroll, and d.budget by joining Departments and Employees on d.dept_name = e.department, grouped by d.dept_name and d.budget.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS emp_count, SUM(e.salary) AS total_payroll, d.budget FROM Departments d INNER JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_name, d.budget;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Calculate total committed hours and headcount per project initiative
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display p.project_name, p.status, COUNT(ep.emp_id) AS assigned_staff, and SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_weekly_hours by joining Projects and Employee_Projects on project_id, grouped by p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, p.status, COUNT(ep.emp_id) AS assigned_staff, SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_weekly_hours FROM Projects p INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Count projects and cumulative initiative investment per department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display d.dept_name, COUNT(p.project_id) AS projects_count, and SUM(p.budget) AS total_project_budget by joining Departments and Projects on dept_id, grouped by d.dept_name.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(p.project_id) AS projects_count, SUM(p.budget) AS total_project_budget FROM Departments d INNER JOIN Projects p ON d.dept_id = p.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_name;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Identify employees with heavy cross-project workloads (> 30 total hours)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, and SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_weekly_hours by joining Employees and Employee_Projects on emp_id, grouped by e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, having total_weekly_hours > 30.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_weekly_hours FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department HAVING SUM(ep.hours_allocated) > 30;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Audit department compensation burn: Total annual payroll vs budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display d.dept_name, (SUM(e.salary) * 12) AS annual_payroll, d.budget AS annual_budget from Departments d INNER JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_name, d.budget HAVING (SUM(e.salary) * 12) > (d.budget * 0.5);
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, (SUM(e.salary) * 12) AS annual_payroll, d.budget AS annual_budget FROM Departments d INNER JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_name, d.budget HAVING (SUM(e.salary) * 12) > (d.budget * 0.5);

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Compute average experience and average salary of teams assigned to each project
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display p.project_name, ROUND(AVG(e.experience), 1) AS avg_team_exp, and ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_team_salary by joining Projects, Employee_Projects, and Employees, grouped by p.project_id, p.project_name.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, ROUND(AVG(e.experience), 1) AS avg_team_exp, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_team_salary FROM Projects p INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id INNER JOIN Employees e ON ep.emp_id = e.emp_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Count distinct projects and distinct reviews per employee
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ep.project_id) AS projects_assigned, and COUNT(DISTINCT pr.review_id) AS reviews_received by LEFT JOINing Employees with Employee_Projects and Performance_Reviews, grouped by e.emp_id, e.emp_name.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ep.project_id) AS projects_assigned, COUNT(DISTINCT pr.review_id) AS reviews_received FROM Employees e LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id LEFT JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_name;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Identify top 3 employees by total project hours worked
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, e.department, and SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_hours by joining Employees and Employee_Projects on emp_id, grouped by e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, ordered by total_hours descending, limited to 3 employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, SUM(ep.hours_allocated) AS total_hours FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department ORDER BY total_hours DESC LIMIT 3;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Calculate total bonuses awarded per department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.department, COUNT(pr.review_id) AS reviewed_count, and SUM(pr.bonus) AS total_department_bonuses by joining Employees and Performance_Reviews on emp_id, grouped by e.department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.department, COUNT(pr.review_id) AS reviewed_count, SUM(pr.bonus) AS total_department_bonuses FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id GROUP BY e.department;

snapshot.subtopic: Aggregations & Analytical Filtering over Joined Relations
snapshot.title: Projects where assigned team members average a performance rating of at least 4.0
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display p.project_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ep.emp_id) AS staff_count, and ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_team_rating by joining Projects p, Employee_Projects ep, and Performance_Reviews pr, grouped by p.project_id, p.project_name, having avg_team_rating >= 4.0.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ep.emp_id) AS staff_count, ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_team_rating FROM Projects p INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON ep.emp_id = pr.emp_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name HAVING AVG(pr.rating) >= 4.0;

snapshot.title: Find employees earning strictly more than the company-wide average salary
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees whose salary is greater than the overall average salary across all employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees);

snapshot.title: Identify corporate initiatives with above-average budget allocations
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and budget for projects whose budget is greater than the average project budget.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, project_name, budget FROM Projects WHERE budget > (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM Projects);

snapshot.title: Retrieve employee details for the company's highest earner
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for the employee(s) who earn the maximum salary in the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees);

snapshot.title: Project company average salary alongside individual employee compensation
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display emp_name, salary, and (SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM Employees) AS company_avg_salary for all employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, salary, (SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) FROM Employees) AS company_avg_salary FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Calculate budget deficit from the maximum project investment
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_name, budget, and ((SELECT MAX(budget) FROM Projects) - budget) AS budget_gap for all projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_name, budget, ((SELECT MAX(budget) FROM Projects) - budget) AS budget_gap FROM Projects;

snapshot.title: Filter performance reviews with above-average bonus awards
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Performance_Reviews to display review_id, emp_id, rating, and bonus for reviews where bonus is strictly greater than the average bonus awarded across all reviews.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT review_id, emp_id, rating, bonus FROM Performance_Reviews WHERE bonus > (SELECT AVG(bonus) FROM Performance_Reviews);

snapshot.title: Find employees earning strictly more than the IT department average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees earning more than the average salary of the 'IT' department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees WHERE department = 'IT');

snapshot.title: Identify departments endowed with above-average operating budgets
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_id, dept_name, location, and budget for departments whose budget exceeds the average departmental budget.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, location, budget FROM Departments WHERE budget > (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM Departments);

snapshot.title: Retrieve all entry-level staff possessing the minimum recorded experience
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and experience for employees having the minimum experience in the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, experience FROM Employees WHERE experience = (SELECT MIN(experience) FROM Employees);

snapshot.title: Find initiatives launched prior to the kickoff of Cloud Migration
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, dept_id, and start_date for projects whose start_date is strictly earlier than the start_date of the 'Cloud Migration' project.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, project_name, dept_id, start_date FROM Projects WHERE start_date < (SELECT start_date FROM Projects WHERE project_name = 'Cloud Migration');

snapshot.title: Find employees working in departments located in Bengaluru
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees whose department is located in 'Bengaluru', using a subquery with IN.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department FROM Employees WHERE department IN (SELECT dept_name FROM Departments WHERE location = 'Bengaluru');

snapshot.title: Find employees assigned to currently active corporate initiatives
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees who are assigned to at least one project with status 'Active'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department FROM Employees WHERE emp_id IN (SELECT ep.emp_id FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id WHERE p.status = 'Active');

snapshot.title: Find employees who have never received a performance review (NOT IN)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees whose emp_id is NOT IN Performance_Reviews.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT emp_id FROM Performance_Reviews);

snapshot.title: Find projects with zero assigned employees (NOT IN)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and status for projects whose project_id is NOT IN Employee_Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, project_name, status FROM Projects WHERE project_id NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM Employee_Projects);

snapshot.title: Find employees who have achieved a top rating of 5 in any review
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees who received a rating of 5 in at least one performance review.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department FROM Employees WHERE emp_id IN (SELECT emp_id FROM Performance_Reviews WHERE rating = 5);

snapshot.title: Find departments that currently have no assigned employees (NOT IN)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_id, dept_name, and location for departments where dept_name is NOT IN the Employees table.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, location FROM Departments WHERE dept_name NOT IN (SELECT department FROM Employees WHERE department IS NOT NULL);

snapshot.title: Find employees assigned to major capital projects (budget >= 300000)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and salary for employees assigned to any project with budget >= 300000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, salary FROM Employees WHERE emp_id IN (SELECT ep.emp_id FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id WHERE p.budget >= 300000);

snapshot.title: Find projects staffed by high-earning talent (salary > 70000)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and status for projects that have at least one assigned employee earning more than 70000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, project_name, status FROM Projects WHERE project_id IN (SELECT ep.project_id FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Employees e ON ep.emp_id = e.emp_id WHERE e.salary > 70000);

snapshot.title: Find employees with no project assignments using NOT IN
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees whose emp_id is NOT IN Employee_Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department FROM Employees WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT emp_id FROM Employee_Projects);

snapshot.title: Find departments without any active projects (NOT IN)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_id, dept_name, and location for departments whose dept_id is NOT IN active projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dept_id, dept_name, location FROM Departments WHERE dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM Projects WHERE status = 'Active' AND dept_id IS NOT NULL);

snapshot.title: Identify assigned personnel using the correlated EXISTS operator
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees where EXISTS a record in Employee_Projects for that employee.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.emp_id = e.emp_id);

snapshot.title: Find unstaffed employees using the correlated NOT EXISTS operator
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees where NOT EXISTS any project assignment for that employee.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.emp_id = e.emp_id);

snapshot.title: Find departments owning at least one active project (EXISTS)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_id, dept_name, and budget for departments where EXISTS at least one active project in Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget FROM Departments d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Projects p WHERE p.dept_id = d.dept_id AND p.status = 'Active');

snapshot.title: Find departments with zero registered projects (NOT EXISTS)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_id, dept_name, and location for departments where NOT EXISTS any project in Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.location FROM Departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Projects p WHERE p.dept_id = d.dept_id);

snapshot.title: Find employees who earned top ratings with significant bonus payouts (EXISTS)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees where EXISTS a review with rating = 5 and bonus > 20000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id AND pr.rating = 5 AND pr.bonus > 20000);

snapshot.title: Identify employees who have never received a cash bonus (NOT EXISTS)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees where NOT EXISTS any review with a non-null bonus.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary FROM Employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id AND pr.bonus IS NOT NULL);

snapshot.title: Find projects with high-commitment staffing assignments (>= 35 hrs/wk)
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and status for projects where EXISTS a staffing assignment with hours_allocated >= 35.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status FROM Projects p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.project_id = p.project_id AND ep.hours_allocated >= 35);

snapshot.title: Find projects lacking any staff assignments using NOT EXISTS
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and budget for projects where NOT EXISTS any assignment in Employee_Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, p.budget FROM Projects p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.project_id = p.project_id);

snapshot.title: Find staff assigned to mega-budget departments (budget >= 1200000) using EXISTS
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees where EXISTS a department with budget >= 1200000 matching their department name.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Departments d WHERE d.dept_name = e.department AND d.budget >= 1200000);

snapshot.title: Identify employees who have undergone multiple performance evaluations
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees where the count of their records in Performance_Reviews is greater than or equal to 2.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id) >= 2;

snapshot.title: Find employees earning strictly more than their OWN department average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees earning more than the average salary of employees in their own department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(sub.salary) FROM Employees sub WHERE sub.department = e.department);

snapshot.title: Identify the top earner in each corporate department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees who hold the highest salary in their respective department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(sub.salary) FROM Employees sub WHERE sub.department = e.department);

snapshot.title: Find the most senior employee in each office city
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, city, and experience for employees who possess the maximum experience in their office city.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.city, e.experience FROM Employees e WHERE e.experience = (SELECT MAX(sub.experience) FROM Employees sub WHERE sub.city = e.city);

snapshot.title: Find performance reviews with bonuses exceeding the annual cycle average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Performance_Reviews to display review_id, emp_id, review_year, and bonus for reviews where bonus is strictly greater than the average bonus for that specific review_year.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT pr.review_id, pr.emp_id, pr.review_year, pr.bonus FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.bonus > (SELECT AVG(sub.bonus) FROM Performance_Reviews sub WHERE sub.review_year = pr.review_year);

snapshot.title: Find initiatives budgeted higher than their department project average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, dept_id, and budget for projects whose budget exceeds the average project budget of their own department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, p.dept_id, p.budget FROM Projects p WHERE p.budget > (SELECT AVG(sub.budget) FROM Projects sub WHERE sub.dept_id = p.dept_id);

snapshot.title: Correlated subquery in SELECT: Project count assigned to each employee
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.emp_id = e.emp_id) AS total_projects for all employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.emp_id = e.emp_id) AS total_projects FROM Employees e;

snapshot.title: Correlated subquery in SELECT: Lifetime peak rating achieved per employee
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and (SELECT MAX(rating) FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id) AS highest_rating for all employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, (SELECT MAX(rating) FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id) AS highest_rating FROM Employees e;

snapshot.title: Correlated subquery in SELECT: Count active initiatives per department
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Departments to display dept_name, location, and (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Projects p WHERE p.dept_id = d.dept_id AND p.status = 'Active') AS active_projects for all departments.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, d.location, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Projects p WHERE p.dept_id = d.dept_id AND p.status = 'Active') AS active_projects FROM Departments d;

snapshot.title: Find staff earning more than ANY colleague in their department who has less experience
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, and e.experience for employees whose salary is strictly greater than the maximum salary of all junior-tenured colleagues in the same department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, e.experience FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT MAX(sub.salary) FROM Employees sub WHERE sub.department = e.department AND sub.experience < e.experience);

snapshot.title: Identify standout review ratings exceeding the employee's own lifetime average
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Performance_Reviews to display pr.review_id, pr.emp_id, pr.review_year, and pr.rating for reviews where the rating is strictly higher than the employee's career average rating across all reviews.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT pr.review_id, pr.emp_id, pr.review_year, pr.rating FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.rating > (SELECT AVG(sub.rating) FROM Performance_Reviews sub WHERE sub.emp_id = pr.emp_id);

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Filter pre-aggregated department metrics using a derived table
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query using a derived table in the FROM clause that computes department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, and ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_sal from Employees, and outer-filters where avg_sal > 50000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dt.department, dt.emp_count, dt.avg_sal FROM (SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_sal FROM Employees GROUP BY department) dt WHERE dt.avg_sal > 50000;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Query workload totals from a derived staffing aggregation
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query using a derived table from Employee_Projects that calculates emp_id and SUM(hours_allocated) AS total_hours, and outer-filters where total_hours > 35.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dt.emp_id, dt.total_hours FROM (SELECT emp_id, SUM(hours_allocated) AS total_hours FROM Employee_Projects GROUP BY emp_id) dt WHERE dt.total_hours > 35;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Join employee records with a departmental statistics derived table
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query to display e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, and dept_stats.avg_dept_sal by joining Employees e with a derived table computing department and ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_dept_sal.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, dept_stats.avg_dept_sal FROM Employees e INNER JOIN (SELECT department, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_dept_sal FROM Employees GROUP BY department) dept_stats ON e.department = dept_stats.department;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Rank employees by salary difference relative to departmental mean using a derived table
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query joining Employees e with a derived table calculating department average salary, selecting e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, (e.salary - dt.avg_sal) AS diff_from_dept_avg, ordered by diff_from_dept_avg descending.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, (e.salary - dt.avg_sal) AS diff_from_dept_avg FROM Employees e INNER JOIN (SELECT department, ROUND(AVG(salary), 2) AS avg_sal FROM Employees GROUP BY department) dt ON e.department = dt.department ORDER BY diff_from_dept_avg DESC;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Identify appraisal years distributing over 100,000 in bonuses using a derived table
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from a derived table aggregating review_year, COUNT(*) AS reviews_count, and SUM(bonus) AS total_bonus from Performance_Reviews, filtering where total_bonus > 100000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT yt.review_year, yt.reviews_count, yt.total_bonus FROM (SELECT review_year, COUNT(*) AS reviews_count, SUM(bonus) AS total_bonus FROM Performance_Reviews GROUP BY review_year) yt WHERE yt.total_bonus > 100000;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Double-nested subquery: Find employees in the department with the highest average salary
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for employees in the department that holds the highest average salary in the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE department = (SELECT department FROM Employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY AVG(salary) DESC LIMIT 1);

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Nested subquery: Find initiatives belonging to the department with the largest operating budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Projects to display project_id, project_name, and budget for projects belonging to the department with the maximum budget in Departments.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, project_name, budget FROM Projects WHERE dept_id = (SELECT dept_id FROM Departments ORDER BY budget DESC LIMIT 1);

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Multi-level subquery: Find employees assigned to the highest funded active initiative
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, and department for employees assigned to the project with the maximum budget among active projects (status = 'Active').
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department FROM Employees WHERE emp_id IN (SELECT ep.emp_id FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.project_id = (SELECT project_id FROM Projects WHERE status = 'Active' ORDER BY budget DESC LIMIT 1));

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Derived table: Compute employee salary as a percentage of department payroll
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query joining Employees e with a derived table calculating department total payroll, displaying e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, and ROUND((e.salary * 100.0) / dp.total_dept_payroll, 2) AS pct_of_dept_payroll.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, ROUND((e.salary * 100.0) / dp.total_dept_payroll, 2) AS pct_of_dept_payroll FROM Employees e INNER JOIN (SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_dept_payroll FROM Employees GROUP BY department) dp ON e.department = dp.department;

snapshot.subtopic: Derived Tables & Subqueries in the FROM Clause
snapshot.title: Grand Challenge: Identify the single most rewarded employee by cumulative lifetime bonus
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query from Employees to display emp_id, emp_name, department, and salary for the employee who earned the highest cumulative bonus across all performance reviews.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE emp_id = (SELECT emp_id FROM Performance_Reviews GROUP BY emp_id ORDER BY SUM(bonus) DESC LIMIT 1);

snapshot.title: Q1. Employees Above a Salary Threshold
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees whose salary strictly exceeds 50,000 INR. Display employee ID, full name, department, and salary.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary > 50000;

snapshot.title: Q2. Employees Within a Salary Range
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees whose salary is between 30,000 and 60,000, inclusive. Display their names and salaries.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary BETWEEN 30000 AND 60000;

snapshot.title: Q3. Employees Matching Multiple Conditions
snapshot.problemStatement: Find all employees who work in the 'IT' department and earn a salary greater than 50,000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE department = 'IT' AND salary > 50000;

snapshot.title: Q4. Employees from Selected Cities
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees who live in Hyderabad or Chennai and have at least 3 years of work experience.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE city IN ('Hyderabad', 'Chennai') AND experience >= 3;

snapshot.title: Q5. Names Matching a Pattern
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees whose names start with the letter 'A' or end with the letter 'a'. Display the employee ID and full name.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name FROM Employees WHERE emp_name LIKE 'A%' OR emp_name LIKE '%a';

snapshot.title: Q6. Total Employee Count
snapshot.problemStatement: Return the total number of employees currently recorded in the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_employees FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Q7. Average Salary by Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Display each department and its average salary, ordered from highest average salary to lowest.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM Employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;

snapshot.title: Q8. Departments with More Than Three Employees
snapshot.problemStatement: Display department names and their employee counts, including only departments that have more than 3 employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM Employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

snapshot.title: Q9. Highest and Lowest Salary
snapshot.problemStatement: Return the maximum salary, minimum salary, and the salary difference (spread) across the entire company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) - MIN(salary) AS salary_difference FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Q10. Total Salary Expense by Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Display each department and the sum of its employee salaries, aliased as total_salary_expense.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_salary_expense FROM Employees GROUP BY department;

snapshot.title: Q11. Cities with High Average Salaries
snapshot.problemStatement: Find office cities whose average employee salary strictly exceeds 45,000 INR.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT city, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM Employees GROUP BY city HAVING AVG(salary) > 45000;

snapshot.title: Q12. Department Salary Statistics
snapshot.problemStatement: For every department, display the employee count, average salary, maximum salary, and minimum salary.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MIN(salary) AS min_salary FROM Employees GROUP BY department;

snapshot.title: Q13. Employee and Department Details
snapshot.problemStatement: Display each employee's name, salary, department name, and department location by joining Employees with Departments.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.salary, d.dept_name, d.location FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name;

snapshot.title: Q14. Employees Without Project Assignments
snapshot.problemStatement: Find all employees who have not been assigned to any project in the Employee_Projects table.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id WHERE ep.project_id IS NULL;

snapshot.title: Q15. Projects Without Employees
snapshot.problemStatement: List projects that currently have no employee assignments recorded in Employee_Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status FROM Projects p LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id WHERE ep.emp_id IS NULL;

snapshot.title: Q16. Employees Assigned to Multiple Projects
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees assigned to more than one distinct project. Show their names and project counts.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ep.project_id) AS project_count FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ep.project_id) > 1;

snapshot.title: Q17. Employee Project Details
snapshot.problemStatement: Display employee name, project name, assigned role, and hours allocated by joining Employees, Employee_Projects, and Projects.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, p.project_name, ep.assigned_role, ep.hours_allocated FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id;

snapshot.title: Q18. Department Employee Counts Including Empty Departments
snapshot.problemStatement: List every department and its total employee count, including departments with zero employees.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS employee_count FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_name;

snapshot.title: Q19. Employees Sharing the Same Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Find pairs of distinct employees who belong to the same department. Avoid duplicate pairs and prevent pairing an employee with themselves.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS employee_1, e2.emp_name AS employee_2, e1.department FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.department = e2.department AND e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Q20. Employees Earning More Than Their Department Head
snapshot.problemStatement: Compare employee salaries against their department head's salary. Return employees whose salary is strictly higher than their department head.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, mgr.emp_name AS dept_head_name, mgr.salary AS dept_head_salary FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name INNER JOIN Employees mgr ON d.dept_head = mgr.emp_name WHERE e.salary > mgr.salary;

snapshot.title: Q21. Cross-Department Collaboration
snapshot.problemStatement: Find pairs of employees assigned to the same project who come from different departments. Avoid duplicate pairs.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT ep1.project_id, e1.emp_name AS employee_1, e1.department AS dept_1, e2.emp_name AS employee_2, e2.department AS dept_2 FROM Employee_Projects ep1 INNER JOIN Employee_Projects ep2 ON ep1.project_id = ep2.project_id AND ep1.emp_id < ep2.emp_id INNER JOIN Employees e1 ON ep1.emp_id = e1.emp_id INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON ep2.emp_id = e2.emp_id WHERE e1.department <> e2.department;

snapshot.title: Q22. Projects with Total Allocated Hours
snapshot.problemStatement: Display each project name and the sum of hours allocated across assigned employees. Include projects with 0 hours allocated.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) AS total_hours FROM Projects p LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name;

snapshot.title: Q23. Employees with Perfect Performance Ratings
snapshot.problemStatement: Display employee name, department, review year, and rating for employees who received a rating of 5 in any performance review.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, pr.review_year, pr.rating FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id WHERE pr.rating = 5;

snapshot.title: Q24. Most Recent Performance Review per Employee
snapshot.problemStatement: For every employee who has received at least one review, display their name, department, latest review year, and latest rating.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, pr.review_year, pr.rating FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id WHERE pr.review_id = (SELECT pr2.review_id FROM Performance_Reviews pr2 WHERE pr2.emp_id = pr.emp_id ORDER BY pr2.review_year DESC, pr2.review_id DESC LIMIT 1);

snapshot.title: Q25. Employees Earning Above Company Average
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees whose salary is strictly greater than the overall company average salary.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Employees);

snapshot.title: Q26. Second Highest Salary Without LIMIT
snapshot.problemStatement: Find the second highest distinct salary across all employees without using the LIMIT clause.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees);

snapshot.title: Q27. Employees in Departments with Above-Average Budgets
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees who belong to departments whose budget is greater than the average department budget across the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees WHERE department IN (SELECT dept_name FROM Departments WHERE budget > (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM Departments));

snapshot.title: Q28. Employees Assigned to High-Budget Projects
snapshot.problemStatement: Find distinct employees assigned to any project whose budget exceeds 250,000 INR.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE e.emp_id IN (SELECT ep.emp_id FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Projects p ON ep.project_id = p.project_id WHERE p.budget > 250000);

snapshot.title: Q29. Department with the Highest Total Payroll
snapshot.problemStatement: Find the single department that has the highest total salary expense in the company.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, SUM(salary) AS total_payroll FROM Employees GROUP BY department ORDER BY total_payroll DESC LIMIT 1;

snapshot.title: Q30. Employees Earning Above Their Department Average
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees who earn more than the average salary of their own specific department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM Employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department);

snapshot.title: Q31. Employees Without Any Performance Reviews
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees who have no review entries recorded in Performance_Reviews using a NOT EXISTS subquery.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, e.department FROM Employees e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Performance_Reviews pr WHERE pr.emp_id = e.emp_id);

snapshot.title: Q32. Projects Staffed Exclusively by IT Employees
snapshot.problemStatement: Find projects that are staffed exclusively by employees from the 'IT' department (must have at least one assigned employee and zero non-IT employees).
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name FROM Projects p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep WHERE ep.project_id = p.project_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Employees e ON ep.emp_id = e.emp_id WHERE ep.project_id = p.project_id AND e.department <> 'IT');

snapshot.title: Q33. Third Highest Distinct Salary Without LIMIT
snapshot.problemStatement: Find the third highest distinct salary across all employees without using the LIMIT clause.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS third_highest_salary FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employees));

snapshot.title: Q34. Employees Working More Hours Than the Project Average
snapshot.problemStatement: For each project assignment, find employees whose allocated hours strictly exceed the average allocated hours for that project.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT ep.project_id, e.emp_name, ep.hours_allocated FROM Employee_Projects ep INNER JOIN Employees e ON ep.emp_id = e.emp_id WHERE ep.hours_allocated > (SELECT AVG(ep2.hours_allocated) FROM Employee_Projects ep2 WHERE ep2.project_id = ep.project_id);

snapshot.title: Q35. Top 3 Highest Earners Overall
snapshot.problemStatement: Display the top 3 highest-earning employees in the company, showing employee name, department, and salary.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3;

snapshot.title: Q36. Highest Earner in Each Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Display the employee name, department, and salary for the highest earner in each department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary FROM Employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM Employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department);

snapshot.title: Q37. Dense Rank of Salaries by Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Using SQL window functions, assign a dense rank to employees within each department ordered by salary descending.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS dept_salary_rank FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Q38. Employees with Identical Salaries
snapshot.problemStatement: Find pairs of distinct employees who earn the exact same salary. Avoid duplicate pairings.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e1.emp_name AS employee_1, e2.emp_name AS employee_2, e1.salary FROM Employees e1 INNER JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.salary = e2.salary AND e1.emp_id < e2.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Q39. Bottom 2 Lowest Earners in the Company
snapshot.problemStatement: Find the 2 employees with the lowest salaries in the company, ordered from lowest salary upwards.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY salary ASC LIMIT 2;

snapshot.subtopic: Part 6 — Duplicate Detection and Data Quality
snapshot.title: Q40. Find Duplicate Office Locations Across Departments
snapshot.problemStatement: Find any office locations that appear more than once across the Departments table, along with their frequency count.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT location, COUNT(*) AS dept_count FROM Departments GROUP BY location HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

snapshot.subtopic: Part 6 — Duplicate Detection and Data Quality
snapshot.title: Q41. Find Departments Without Any Employees
snapshot.problemStatement: Find departments in the Departments table that currently have no assigned employees in the Employees table.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.location FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department WHERE e.emp_id IS NULL;

snapshot.subtopic: Part 6 — Duplicate Detection and Data Quality
snapshot.title: Q42. Identify Inactive Projects (Zero Assigned Hours)
snapshot.problemStatement: Find projects that either have no assigned employees or have a total of 0 allocated hours.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status FROM Projects p LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name, p.status HAVING COUNT(ep.emp_id) = 0 OR COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) = 0;

snapshot.subtopic: Part 6 — Duplicate Detection and Data Quality
snapshot.title: Q43. Detect Salary Outliers within Department
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees whose salary is more than 30% higher than the average salary of their own department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, ROUND(sub.avg_dept_sal, 2) AS dept_avg_salary FROM Employees e INNER JOIN (SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_dept_sal FROM Employees GROUP BY department) sub ON e.department = sub.department WHERE e.salary > sub.avg_dept_sal * 1.3;

snapshot.title: Q44. Salary Review Eligibility
snapshot.problemStatement: Find employees in Finance or IT with at least 5 years of experience earning less than 70,000 INR, who qualify for a mid-year compensation review.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, department, experience, salary FROM Employees WHERE department IN ('Finance', 'IT') AND experience >= 5 AND salary < 70000;

snapshot.title: Q45. Departments Exceeding Annual Salary Budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Compare each department's total annualized payroll (monthly salary * 12) against its annual budget. Return departments where annual payroll strictly exceeds the budget.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, SUM(e.salary * 12) AS annual_payroll, d.budget FROM Departments d INNER JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_name, d.budget HAVING SUM(e.salary * 12) > d.budget;

snapshot.title: Q46. Workload Classification by Total Allocated Hours
snapshot.problemStatement: Calculate total weekly hours allocated to each employee across all projects and classify their workload into tiers: 'Unassigned' (0 hours), 'Light Workload' (under 25 hours), 'Moderate Workload' (25 to 35 hours), and 'Heavy Workload' (over 35 hours).
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) AS total_hours, CASE WHEN COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) = 0 THEN 'Unassigned' WHEN SUM(ep.hours_allocated) < 25 THEN 'Light Workload' WHEN SUM(ep.hours_allocated) <= 35 THEN 'Moderate Workload' ELSE 'Heavy Workload' END AS workload_tier FROM Employees e LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON e.emp_id = ep.emp_id GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_name;

snapshot.title: Q47. Salary Tier Classification
snapshot.problemStatement: Classify each employee's salary into tiers: 'Low' for salaries below 35,000, 'Medium' for salaries between 35,000 and 60,000 inclusive, and 'High' for salaries above 60,000.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary, CASE WHEN salary < 35000 THEN 'Low' WHEN salary <= 60000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'High' END AS salary_tier FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Q48. Experience-Based Seniority Tier
snapshot.problemStatement: Classify employees into seniority tiers based on years of experience: 'Fresher' (under 2 years), 'Junior' (2 to 4 years), 'Mid-Level' (5 to 8 years), and 'Senior' (9 or more years).
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, experience, CASE WHEN experience < 2 THEN 'Fresher' WHEN experience <= 4 THEN 'Junior' WHEN experience <= 8 THEN 'Mid-Level' ELSE 'Senior' END AS seniority_tier FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Q49. Conditional Department Salary Summary
snapshot.problemStatement: For each department, calculate the count of high earners (salary > 50,000) and standard earners (salary <= 50,000) using conditional aggregation with CASE expressions.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, SUM(CASE WHEN salary > 50000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_earners, SUM(CASE WHEN salary <= 50000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS standard_earners FROM Employees GROUP BY department;

snapshot.title: Q50. Performance-Based Bonus Recommendation
snapshot.problemStatement: Recommend a bonus category for each reviewed employee based on their rating: rating of 5 is 'Exceptional', rating of 4 is 'Strong', rating of 3 is 'Satisfactory', and anything below 3 is 'Needs Improvement'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, pr.review_year, pr.rating, CASE WHEN pr.rating = 5 THEN 'Exceptional' WHEN pr.rating = 4 THEN 'Strong' WHEN pr.rating = 3 THEN 'Satisfactory' ELSE 'Needs Improvement' END AS recommendation FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Map office cities into operational zones using simple CASE
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a SQL query using a simple CASE expression to map employee office cities into operational zones: 'Hyderabad' and 'Vijayawada' to 'South-Central', 'Chennai' to 'South-Coastal', 'Bengaluru' to 'South-Tech', and any other location to 'Other Zone'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, city, CASE city WHEN 'Hyderabad' THEN 'South-Central' WHEN 'Vijayawada' THEN 'South-Central' WHEN 'Chennai' THEN 'South-Coastal' WHEN 'Bengaluru' THEN 'South-Tech' ELSE 'Other Zone' END AS operational_zone FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Generate a binary recent hire indicator using searched CASE
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a query using a searched CASE statement that flags whether an employee was hired recently. Return a flag is_recent_hire that evaluates to 1 if joining_year is 2023 or later, and 0 otherwise.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, joining_year, CASE WHEN joining_year >= 2023 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_recent_hire FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Classify project delivery urgency with explicit ELSE fallback
snapshot.problemStatement: Display project name, status, and delivery_urgency. If status is 'Active', urgency is 'In Progress'; if status is 'Planning', urgency is 'Upcoming'; for all other statuses, explicitly return 'Archive / Standby' using the ELSE clause.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_name, status, CASE status WHEN 'Active' THEN 'In Progress' WHEN 'Planning' THEN 'Upcoming' ELSE 'Archive / Standby' END AS delivery_urgency FROM Projects;

snapshot.title: Identify fast-track talent using compound boolean conditions
snapshot.problemStatement: Write a query to evaluate employee career profiles. If an employee is aged 25 or younger (age <= 25) AND has at least 2 years of experience (experience >= 2), designate them as 'Fast Track Candidate'; otherwise label as 'Standard Profile'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, age, experience, CASE WHEN age <= 25 AND experience >= 2 THEN 'Fast Track Candidate' ELSE 'Standard Profile' END AS career_profile FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Categorize workforce into demographic age brackets
snapshot.problemStatement: Categorize employees into age cohorts: 'Under 25' for ages under 25, '25 to 29' for ages 25 through 29, and '30 and Above' for ages 30 and older. Display emp_id, emp_name, age, and age_group.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_id, emp_name, age, CASE WHEN age < 25 THEN 'Under 25' WHEN age <= 29 THEN '25 to 29' ELSE '30 and Above' END AS age_group FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Apply department-specific compensation scale status
snapshot.problemStatement: Classify employees into compensation scales: If an employee belongs to the 'IT' department and earns 50,000 or more, label as 'Tech Core Scale'; if in 'IT' and earns under 50,000, label as 'Tech Entry Scale'; for all non-IT employees, label as 'General Corporate Scale'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary, CASE WHEN department = 'IT' AND salary >= 50000 THEN 'Tech Core Scale' WHEN department = 'IT' THEN 'Tech Entry Scale' ELSE 'General Corporate Scale' END AS pay_scale_status FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Classify employee tenure into organizational loyalty brackets
snapshot.problemStatement: Determine employee loyalty tiers based on their joining year: 'Veteran' if joined before 2020 (joining_year < 2020), 'Established' if joined between 2020 and 2022 inclusive, and 'New Hire' if joined in 2023 or later. Display emp_name, joining_year, and loyalty_tier.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, joining_year, CASE WHEN joining_year < 2020 THEN 'Veteran' WHEN joining_year <= 2022 THEN 'Established' ELSE 'New Hire' END AS loyalty_tier FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Group organizational departments into broad corporate divisions
snapshot.problemStatement: Map each department in the Departments table into an enterprise division: 'IT' and 'R&D' to 'Technology & Innovation'; 'Sales' and 'Marketing' to 'Growth & Revenue'; 'Finance' and 'Legal' to 'Governance & Capital'; and all others to 'Operations & Support'. Display dept_name and division.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT dept_name, CASE WHEN dept_name IN ('IT', 'R&D') THEN 'Technology & Innovation' WHEN dept_name IN ('Sales', 'Marketing') THEN 'Growth & Revenue' WHEN dept_name IN ('Finance', 'Legal') THEN 'Governance & Capital' ELSE 'Operations & Support' END AS division FROM Departments;

snapshot.title: Sort employee roster in custom executive presentation order
snapshot.problemStatement: Sort employees by department according to executive presentation priority rather than alphabetical order: 'IT' first, followed by 'Finance', 'Marketing', 'Sales', and finally 'HR'. Break ties within each department by salary descending. Display emp_name, department, and salary.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary FROM Employees ORDER BY CASE department WHEN 'IT' THEN 1 WHEN 'Finance' THEN 2 WHEN 'Marketing' THEN 3 WHEN 'Sales' THEN 4 WHEN 'HR' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END, salary DESC;

snapshot.title: Audit performance bonuses with NULL-safe evaluation
snapshot.problemStatement: Generate a bonus distribution audit from Performance_Reviews. For each review, display review_id, emp_id, rating, bonus, and payout_status: If bonus IS NULL or 0, display 'No Bonus Awarded'; If bonus is under 15,000, display 'Standard Bonus'; Otherwise display 'High Performance Bonus'.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT review_id, emp_id, rating, bonus, CASE WHEN bonus IS NULL OR bonus = 0 THEN 'No Bonus Awarded' WHEN bonus < 15000 THEN 'Standard Bonus' ELSE 'High Performance Bonus' END AS payout_status FROM Performance_Reviews;

snapshot.title: Filter by a CASE-derived classification using an outer subquery
snapshot.problemStatement: Classify employee salaries into pay grades: 'Executive Pay' (salary >= 75000), 'Mid Pay' (salary between 40000 and 74999), and 'Junior Pay' (salary < 40000). Wrap this logic in an outer query or CTE to filter and return ONLY employees classified as 'Executive Pay'. Display emp_name, department, salary, and pay_grade.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, department, salary, pay_grade FROM (SELECT emp_name, department, salary, CASE WHEN salary >= 75000 THEN 'Executive Pay' WHEN salary >= 40000 THEN 'Mid Pay' ELSE 'Junior Pay' END AS pay_grade FROM Employees) classified WHERE pay_grade = 'Executive Pay';

snapshot.title: Order corporate initiatives by project lifecycle status urgency
snapshot.problemStatement: List all projects sorted by operational status urgency: 'Active' first, 'Planning' second, and 'Completed' last. Break ties by project budget in descending order. Display project_name, status, and budget.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT project_name, status, budget FROM Projects ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'Active' THEN 1 WHEN 'Planning' THEN 2 WHEN 'Completed' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, budget DESC;

snapshot.title: Count total and senior staff per city using COUNT(CASE WHEN ...)
snapshot.problemStatement: For each city, calculate the total number of employees, and count how many have 5 or more years of experience using COUNT(CASE WHEN experience >= 5 THEN 1 END). Display city, total_employees, and senior_count.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS total_employees, COUNT(CASE WHEN experience >= 5 THEN 1 END) AS senior_count FROM Employees GROUP BY city;

snapshot.title: Calculate total payroll expenditure split across experience brackets
snapshot.problemStatement: In a single summary query without a GROUP BY clause, compute the total salary expense for junior employees (experience < 4, aliased as junior_payroll) and senior employees (experience >= 4, aliased as senior_payroll).
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN experience < 4 THEN salary ELSE 0 END) AS junior_payroll, SUM(CASE WHEN experience >= 4 THEN salary ELSE 0 END) AS senior_payroll FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Compare low, mid, and high salary bands per department
snapshot.problemStatement: For each department, display the count of employees in three salary tiers: tier_low (salary < 35000), tier_mid (salary between 35000 and 60000 inclusive), and tier_high (salary > 60000). Group by department.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, SUM(CASE WHEN salary < 35000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tier_low, SUM(CASE WHEN salary BETWEEN 35000 AND 60000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tier_mid, SUM(CASE WHEN salary > 60000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tier_high FROM Employees GROUP BY department;

snapshot.title: Compute conditional average salary for IT versus business departments
snapshot.problemStatement: Compute the company-wide average salary of IT employees versus all non-IT department employees in a single row summary. Display avg_it_salary and avg_non_it_salary, both rounded to 2 decimal places.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN department = 'IT' THEN salary END), 2) AS avg_it_salary, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN department <> 'IT' THEN salary END), 2) AS avg_non_it_salary FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Calculate department high earner percentage with zero-division guard
snapshot.problemStatement: For each department, calculate the percentage of employees earning 50,000 or more. Display department, total_staff, high_earner_count, and high_earner_percentage (rounded to 1 decimal place). Use a CASE expression to prevent division-by-zero errors if total_staff is 0.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS total_staff, SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_earner_count, ROUND(CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE (SUM(CASE WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*)) * 100.0 END, 1) AS high_earner_percentage FROM Employees GROUP BY department;

snapshot.title: Categorize employee work arrangement using joined department headquarters
snapshot.problemStatement: Join Employees with Departments on e.department = d.dept_name. Categorize each employee's work model: If the employee's office city matches the department's primary location, label as 'Colocated HQ'; otherwise label as 'Regional Branch'. Display emp_name, department, employee city, department location, and work_model.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.city, d.location, CASE WHEN e.city = d.location THEN 'Colocated HQ' ELSE 'Regional Branch' END AS work_model FROM Employees e INNER JOIN Departments d ON e.department = d.dept_name;

snapshot.title: Classify project resource intensity via aggregated staffing allocations
snapshot.problemStatement: Join Projects with Employee_Projects to calculate total allocated hours and assigned headcount for every project. Classify resource intensity: If headcount is 0 OR total hours is 0 -> 'Unstaffed'; If total hours < 50 -> 'Low Intensity'; If total hours <= 80 -> 'Medium Intensity'; Otherwise -> 'High Intensity'. Display project_name, total_hours, staff_count, and intensity_rating.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) AS total_hours, COUNT(ep.emp_id) AS staff_count, CASE WHEN COUNT(ep.emp_id) = 0 OR COALESCE(SUM(ep.hours_allocated), 0) = 0 THEN 'Unstaffed' WHEN SUM(ep.hours_allocated) < 50 THEN 'Low Intensity' WHEN SUM(ep.hours_allocated) <= 80 THEN 'Medium Intensity' ELSE 'High Intensity' END AS intensity_rating FROM Projects p LEFT JOIN Employee_Projects ep ON p.project_id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name;

snapshot.title: Classify employee salary standing against correlated department averages
snapshot.problemStatement: Classify each employee's salary standing relative to their own department's average salary: If salary is strictly greater than 115% of the department average, label as 'Above Dept Average'; If between 85% and 115% inclusive, label as 'At Dept Average'; If below 85%, label as 'Below Dept Average'. Display emp_name, department, salary, and salary_standing.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_name, e.department, e.salary, CASE WHEN e.salary > (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM Employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department) * 1.15 THEN 'Above Dept Average' WHEN e.salary >= (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM Employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department) * 0.85 THEN 'At Dept Average' ELSE 'Below Dept Average' END AS salary_standing FROM Employees e;

snapshot.title: Generate project capital scale report comparing project versus department budget
snapshot.problemStatement: Join Projects with Departments on dept_id. Classify project_scale based on what share of the owning department's budget the project consumes: If project budget exceeds 30% of department budget, label as 'Major Capital Project'; If between 15% and 30% inclusive, label as 'Significant Project'; Otherwise 'Routine Department Project'. Display project_name, dept_name, project_budget, dept_budget, and project_scale.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT p.project_name, d.dept_name, p.budget AS project_budget, d.budget AS dept_budget, CASE WHEN p.budget > d.budget * 0.30 THEN 'Major Capital Project' WHEN p.budget >= d.budget * 0.15 THEN 'Significant Project' ELSE 'Routine Department Project' END AS project_scale FROM Projects p INNER JOIN Departments d ON p.dept_id = d.dept_id;

snapshot.title: Assess employee retention risk using nested CASE expressions
snapshot.problemStatement: Evaluate retention risk using a nested CASE expression. For employees with 6 or more years of experience: if salary is under 60,000 label as 'High Flight Risk (Underpaid Veteran)', else 'Key Retained Leader'. For employees with under 6 years of experience: if salary is under 30,000 label as 'Entry Flight Risk', else 'Standard Stable'. Display emp_name, experience, salary, and retention_assessment.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, experience, salary, CASE WHEN experience >= 6 THEN CASE WHEN salary < 60000 THEN 'High Flight Risk (Underpaid Veteran)' ELSE 'Key Retained Leader' END ELSE CASE WHEN salary < 30000 THEN 'Entry Flight Risk' ELSE 'Standard Stable' END END AS retention_assessment FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Implement priority-ordered tier designations with short-circuiting logic
snapshot.problemStatement: Assign professional career designations where overlapping qualifications exist. The most prestigious tier must take precedence: 1) experience >= 8 AND salary >= 75000 -> 'Leadership Tier'; 2) experience >= 6 OR salary >= 60000 -> 'Senior Contributor'; 3) experience >= 3 -> 'Core Professional'; 4) Else -> 'Associate'. Display emp_name, experience, salary, and tier_designation.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT emp_name, experience, salary, CASE WHEN experience >= 8 AND salary >= 75000 THEN 'Leadership Tier' WHEN experience >= 6 OR salary >= 60000 THEN 'Senior Contributor' WHEN experience >= 3 THEN 'Core Professional' ELSE 'Associate' END AS tier_designation FROM Employees;

snapshot.title: Build comprehensive appraisal audit handling outer joins and NULL bonuses
snapshot.problemStatement: Left join Employees with Performance_Reviews to evaluate appraisal status across all employees: If the employee has never been reviewed (pr.review_id IS NULL) -> 'Pending Initial Review'; If rating >= 4 AND bonus IS NOT NULL -> 'Top Performer (Bonus Awarded)'; If rating >= 4 AND bonus IS NULL -> 'High Rating (No Cash Bonus)'; Else -> 'Standard Rating (No Cash Bonus)'. Display emp_id, emp_name, review_year, rating, and appraisal_status.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_name, pr.review_year, pr.rating, CASE WHEN pr.review_id IS NULL THEN 'Pending Initial Review' WHEN pr.rating >= 4 AND pr.bonus IS NOT NULL THEN 'Top Performer (Bonus Awarded)' WHEN pr.rating >= 4 AND pr.bonus IS NULL THEN 'High Rating (No Cash Bonus)' ELSE 'Standard Rating (No Cash Bonus)' END AS appraisal_status FROM Employees e LEFT JOIN Performance_Reviews pr ON e.emp_id = pr.emp_id;

snapshot.title: Generate departmental restructuring matrix based on headcount and budget health
snapshot.problemStatement: Evaluate enterprise department health by left joining Departments with Employees. Evaluate total staff and annualized payroll (SUM(salary * 12)): If headcount is 0 -> 'Vacant Department - Urgent Staffing'; If headcount >= 5 AND annualized payroll > budget -> 'Overstaffed & Overbudget'; If annualized payroll > budget -> 'Overbudget Warning'; If headcount <= 2 -> 'Undermanned Unit'; Else -> 'Balanced Operations'. Display dept_name, staff_count, annual_payroll, budget, and restructure_priority.
snapshot.expectedSql: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS staff_count, COALESCE(SUM(e.salary * 12), 0) AS annual_payroll, d.budget, CASE WHEN COUNT(e.emp_id) = 0 THEN 'Vacant Department - Urgent Staffing' WHEN COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 5 AND SUM(e.salary * 12) > d.budget THEN 'Overstaffed & Overbudget' WHEN SUM(e.salary * 12) > d.budget THEN 'Overbudget Warning' WHEN COUNT(e.emp_id) <= 2 THEN 'Undermanned Unit' ELSE 'Balanced Operations' END AS restructure_priority FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Employees e ON d.dept_name = e.department GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget;
